utterances.text: So this person is John Gerns, who was together with us on this mission. We now have a date, end of August 1996. And I took this picture, and John Gerns was a crime scene technician, and at this moment he's collecting samples on the walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What kind of samples is he collecting?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible blood traces to check if they are human or not, and also traces of substance to check if there are explosive traces or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Were these samples tested?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same situation then for the first samples that we took at the Kravica warehouse. At this moment the goal was to prepare a thorough forensic mission and only to secure the samples if ever something happened to the location before we would return there. So these ones were just stored and not processed. Maybe only -- maybe only one to check if it was indeed the human blood or not, but in this location it's not the same then in the Kravica warehouse. There is no possibility this place would ever have been used as an animal slaughterhouse. So we were sure it was human.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, 232 in the hard copy, 242 in e-court. What does this photo show?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This a bloodstain on the wall that we took before the crime scene technician could take his sample.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The next page, 233, 243 in e-court. And this photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same situation. A bloodstain on the wall before taking the sample.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next page, 234 in hard copy, 244 in e-court. Now, what particular part of the Dom of Culture are we looking at here, and what are the marks on the wall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the few stairs at the back of this room where the stage is and where most probably the -- the people jammed once the shooting started, and this is an obvious, again, bloodstain on this part of the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And is it correct that a team of forensic experts went back to this site after your initial visit?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And they made a report about their findings from this site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, go to page 235 in hard copy, 245 in e-court. Can you describe what we can see in these photos starting with the black marks that we can see across the bottom half of the photo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is at the back of -- the wall at the back of the room, the very end of it, and the black traces are traces of grenades that were thrown in and exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what are the marks on the right of the photo that we can see up towards the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are also on this one sprays of blood splashed on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page, please, 236 in hard copy and 246 in e-court. We're looking at an aerial image dated 17 July 1995. Did you put the yellow markings on this image, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you describe their significance to us.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the truck was -- was marked on the original one. I added -- and the truck is parked just in front of the blue door, the main entrance door, and the interest of the traces is that they lead also to the rear door, knowing that any cleaning of the inside would necessitate to take the bodies out, both from the front and also from the rear door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, can you orient us on this? We can see a road running on the right-hand side of the image from top to bottom.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Which road is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the asphalt road leading -- going south at the bottom of the picture towards Zvornik and to the top towards the north, Bijeljina. And more or less where the numbering of the picture is, top right, is where the -- just underneath it's where the cafe is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So underneath the number 704.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the location of the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page, please, 237 in hard copy and 247 in e-court. Can you describe what this picture is showing and then tell us the significance of the red arrow.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies from -- of those who were shot inside the Dom, the assumption at that time was that due to the fact that the witness who did hide under the bridge saw a truck with dead bodies inside take this direction indicated to us that the bodies were probably taken to the Branjevo Farm, and the red arrow shows the direction, in fact the path that would be taken by -- by the trucks who brought the bodies to the Branjevo Farm, the farm being just behind the end of the arrows, just behind the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The starting point of the red arrows, is it the building immediately to the right of that? Is that the Dom of Culture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Dom of Culture, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I want to show you another video now - it's 65 ter 40235A - and again have you describe what we can see in this video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is the arrival at the Dom. So here is the front facade. The asphalt road pointing in the direction of Bijeljina. Here again we have the Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you recall what year this footage was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Now we have a certainty of a date. It's 23rd August, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What's that building we just saw?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was the cafe. It's a 360-degree turn. So this is entering the front facade, and here is, in fact -- was a door leading to the inside of the Dom of Culture, but this door had been completely sealed with concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We're at 1 minute, 25, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is the entrance for the smaller area that is the com centre, telephone centre. We didn't do this hole at the hop tight. It was there. This is what could be seen from the -- from this little hole. That's the back of the building. So making a turn. So this is from the -- the cabin of the projectionist, through one of the two -- two holes. So this is the location from where the -- the initial shooting started. That's the staircase going down. The floor had been cleaned, but the cleaning lady was not very thorough, and on the sides there were still shell casings. Shell casings. Shell casings. Also shell casings. So this is from the outside. The cafe just at the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The IFOR troops who we just saw, were they anything to do with your visit?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. They were our escort, this area being part of the Ivandi [phoen] north, but on the so-called Russian sector. For this occasion it was a Russian unit. So that's at the -- at the outside. Still rubber gloves, probably I can expect left over from those who went inside to clean -- to clean the bodies out of -- out of the room. A shell casing. And then we broke the locker and could get inside. So this is inside. It's Peter Nicholson who is filming. The hole from the projectionist. So I don't describe all the traces. They are obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What are we looking at now? This is at 7 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now it's the stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It's 7 minutes, 45 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we're also looking to see if there was some obvious things underneath the stage. There are some pieces of "licna karta," IDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That's at 8 minutes, 55.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shell casing. Shell casing. And a few of the IDs that were found. Only one had -- if I remember well, only one had a name, clear name on it, with a photograph. Yeah, this one. And he was on the missing list of the Red Cross as missing from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It was at 9 minutes and 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I tender that video, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P4307, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, when was the last time you went to the Dom of Culture in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last time was, I think, in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And had the site changed at all from what we saw in that footage?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. In 2002 we could have returned with a team of forensic experts. Like the Kravica situation, everything was absolutely still in place. Only the -- the outside had changed significantly, but the inside, not at all in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's move on to a different area. We'll skip to page 239 in the hard copy of your book, 249 in e-court. Can you explain very briefly what this map shows?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this map shows the location of all the mass graves that existed in the area in -- once the exhumation -- the initial inhumation process was finalised. So that was on 17 July 1995, and this is the situation at the time for the main graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did your investigation indicate that something had happened with those graves in the months after 17 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact is that at the end of the exhumation process conducted by Bill Haglund in 1996, on the main -- the priority was put on the main execution sites. At the end of the year, only 500 -- about 500 bodies had been collected, recovered, though our assumption according to the witness testimonies was that we should have found a much, much larger amount. So there was even an article in "Newsweek" with the title "Genocide Without Corpses." So the question was where the bodies had been taken, especially since the exhumation of the sites clearly indicated that the initial mass graves were much larger than the area where the bodies were found. So there had been a very clear and obvious robbery process of all the bodies in all these primary burial sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And how did you first learn of the secondary sites where these remains had been moved to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh. The first indication came from someone who indicated suspect -- more than suspect spots at the south of the enclave in an area totally remote that is named Zeleni Jadar where this person enabled us, through his indications, to find four secondary mass graves, and additional imagery enabled us to find, in fact, six mass graves at the south of Srebrenica. Those that we suspected came from the main burial site initially located in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: After you located the six sites at Zeleni Jadar with imagery, who then took the initiation and discovered other sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this discovery and also after the confirmation that despite of what was initially thought from the aerial imagery that the site at the dam had also been tampered with, the analysis of all these pictures that existed, though the significance of them had to be pinpointed in order to understand what could be on the picture, so the US government provided us with several pictures that enables us then to go on the ground and check these locations once after another and check if there was inside multiple bodies in order to start exhuming them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's look at a few of those images briefly. Can we go to the next page, 240 in the hard copy and 250 in e-court. Can you tell us which site this is we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one is LZ-2, which is the first of the -- first execution site of Orahovac with one picture showing the situation dated 7 September where we already had the disturbance, but then on a following picture dated 27, one can clearly see that the disturbance doesn't look any longer the same than on 27. So something had happened on this site between the 7th and the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, 241 in the hard copy, 251 in e-court. If you can tell us which site this is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the -- the same Orahovac place but this is LZ-1 and same situation. The disturbance doesn't look any longer the same between the 7th and 27th September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next page, 242 in the hard copy, 252 in e-court. And can you explain again this image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly the same situation but for the Petrovic dam where the disturbance caused by the creation of the grave shows in a different way between the 7th September and the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And are we -- here we're looking at the flat area in front of the dam?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please, 243 in the hard copy, 253 in e-court. Now we're looking at disturbed earth at Kozluk with another split image, the left dated 7 September 1995, the right dated 27 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh. It's exactly the same situation again but this time for the Kozluk site. This is also the reason why on all these sites we could probably find so easily human remains, human bones scattered on the surface, since all this process of removing the bodies with heavy equipment, then they spill out certain number of items. So this one is the disturbance of Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please, 244 in the hard copy, 254 in e-court. This is a single image at the Branjevo Farm, dated 27 September 1995. Now the heading that says "Newly excavated trench" and the identification of a backhoe and a front loader, they were put there by the provider; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. All these marks and the blowups on the yard of the farm, all this is labelled by the provider.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what's significant about this particular image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We already knew the very precise location of the mass grave, and on this one, one can very clearly see where the location is but now it is open again, and inside the yard is also -- it's very fuzzy on the one we have here, but one can see, indeed, a backhoe and also a front loader.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to next page, please, 245 in hard copy, 255 in e-court. Can you tell us which particular site this exhumation is taking place at?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This one is at the Branjevo Farm, and this is a perfect example of the end result we could have at the end of 1996 since the large hole seen on the photograph is the size of the initial mass grave, but it's only on the spot where the three colleagues are standing that a pile of -- a stack of about 100 bodies was left. It was the open thing that was left in this huge mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page, 246 in hard copy and 256 in e-court. Is this the stack of bodies that you just referred to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the stack of bodies that was left at the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page, 247 in hard copy, 257 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the aerial photographs of Glogova, which is -- which comes in a series of -- that could show the entire evolution of this very important site since this site is the grave for not only the bodies coming from the Kravica warehouse but also the bodies of those who were executed in Bratunac town and also of those who were killed along the side of the road when they surrendered, and all of them were taken to Glogova. And this particular photograph dated 30 October shows in fact the disturbance process when -- ongoing since a front loader is still inside one of these mass graves because it's an area of a cluster of several mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And that conclusion that we can see a front loader on the image, that's -- that conclusion was made by the provider again?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The labelling "Front loader" is done by the provider.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The next page, please, 248 in the hard copy, 258 in e-court. If you can briefly describe this and the significance of the yellow arrow we can see pointing to the south.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact this one depicts only the -- the move of the bodies taken from Glogova and shipped to the opposite side of the UN safe area, at the south of it at Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And there's other witnesses who talk more about the connections between those two graves, or those two series of graves.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The connection is done by the results of forensics post-exhumation since a lot of the possibilities exist to then connect the primary sites to -- with the secondary sites, i.e., extremely obvious items, soil analysis, shell casing comparison, various methods that will be entered into detail by another person, Dean Manning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page, 249 in the hard copy, and 259 in e-court. If you can describe what we can see here on this image.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows the area we named Zeleni Jadar. It's totally south of the former enclave, and this shows, in fact, the way these sites have been spread along this small road, scattered in a clear intent that if one is found, we would certainly not be able to find the other ones because this is an extremely remote area, and many of these locations are, in fact, at the edge of a previous confrontation line with a lot of mine fields also in this -- in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please, 250 in the hard copy, and 260 in e-court. Who is the person we can see in this photo, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. This is William Haglund, and we were doing what we call a probe on one of these suspect sites in Zeleni Jadar and could confirm the presence of human remains. Here we see a man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And this is the Zeleni Jadar 4 site; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This is Zeleni Jadar 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And can we go to the next page, please, 251 in the hard copy, 261 in e-court. We can see seven yellow and black circles in this map to the west of Zvornik. Can you explain what these seven circles represent?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These ones are part of suspect sites that we -- we probed each of them in 2007, so this is a cluster along the stretch of road that was the former road going from Zvornik towards Tuzla. It was then a dirt -- a dirt road, remote, out of the normal way to go out to Zvornik. And all those were probed positive and were later exhumed. The bodies of these ones are the ones coming from Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And when you say you probed them in 2007, is that the right year or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what are these seven locations known as?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the Hodzici Road, so HZ. The code sign should be HZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, 252 in hard copy, and 262 in e-court. Are these the same seven sites we were just talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. Again, it shows how -- how spread these -- these places are, the goal of being clearly to scatter all these remains in order to make sure that even if one of these sites could be found, the magnitude of the crime would not be fully understood since there would be a lot of missing bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Look at the next page, 253 in hard copy, 263 in e-court. This map shows four yellow and black circles just below the location Liplje. Can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These ones are also in the area close to Zvornik. We also probed these sites and exhumation. It was in 1997 again, the probing, and the exhumation again enabled the experts to connect these sites with those of the -- the prisoners executed at the dam.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, page 254 in hard copy and 264 in e-court. Are these the four sites that you were just describing?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is this area near Liplje, was that inhabited when you went there and did probes on these locations?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the places where secondary graves are located are all -- were at that time all totally inhabited, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page. It's a map showing nine yellow circles in the area of Cancari.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Cancari valley is a long -- is a long -- in the middle has a long dirt road. It's about 8 kilometres long, the valley. And these spots on this map pinpoint locations of -- a chain of secondary graves, and these ones are the ones coming from the Branjevo -- Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Are they all from the Branjevo Farm or are some of them from another location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These ones are only from the Branjevo Farm. On the -- the entrance of the valley there are three -- three more coming from Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, 256. And, Mr. Ruez, just further up the page, on page 56, at line 9, where you said all the places where secondary graves were located were at that time totally inhabited; is that correct? So people were living round about the locations?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no one living around the locations. The locations were all in areas where the houses were totally destroyed, not habited.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So that's uninhabited; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uninhabited, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. We're looking at page 256. If you can describe what we're looking at in this image.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a picture taken in 1998, and it shows the Cancari valley. At the moment, in fact, the valley becomes a bit larger, but all the houses you can see on this, some of them have already been partially reconstructed, but in 1995 and early 1996, no one was living at all in these places. It would have been much too dangerous to live there before the total end of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We can see a road running from the bottom of the picture right up through the middle. Can you orient us on that? Which direction if you go out the bottom of the picture? Where is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bottom of the picture, this dirt road goes to the Drina valley. So once you are at the Drina valley, if you go south, you would go towards Nova Kasaba; and if you go north, you go to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, 257, 267 in e-court. And these are the Cancari Road sites that you've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So the -- the Drina valley being out of the pictures on the right hand. The first sites where, I mean, maybe three, maybe four, I cannot be sure, are coming from the Kozluk area. This is from one of these that we went immediately to Kozluk after having found the labels and the broken glass and all the others are the Branjevo farm of interest of the picture, again, to show how spread these sites are along this -- this valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we look at the next page -- or actually skip the next page and go to page 259 and 269 in e-court. Can you describe what this is that's in this photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. So this is a helicopter view of the set-up of an exhumation of the secondary mass grave compared with the aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And the next -- the next page, please, 260 in hard copy and 270 in e-court. And which site is it that we're looking at here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Cancari 12, site number 12, and this is a photograph of the first layer of a mass grave. We -- we wished to have this first layer, which is not necessarily even normal way the exhumation is conducted, but in order to have a visual assessment of how -- how the full surface of such a grave would look like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have about maybe 5 to 10 minutes left. I am not sure what time the next break was scheduled for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can continue to quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's go to page 264 in the hard copy and 274 in e-court. Can you explain first what we're looking at here, and second, what date this image was taken on?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture is -- is an extract of the video V550, the video filmed by Zoran Petrovic. The video is -- his video is dated 12 July. And this is at the moment he enters Srebrenica town and where one can see that the central mosque in the centre of Srebrenica town was the main -- two main religious buildings, one being a church, the other one being the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So this is the mosque in the centre of Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As it was after the take-over of the Bosnian Serb Army, the day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page, 265 in hard copy, 275 in e-court. And first if you can tell us what date this photo was taken.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photo was -- I took it in April 1996. The date is on it. It was 16 or 18 April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what does it show?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows the same mosque than the one on the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And how are you able to tell that that's the same mosque as the one we saw on the previous photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's clearly obvious since it is exactly at the same location, centre town, and the only items you could recognise on this one since it has been totally blown up is one part of the roof and one piece of the minaret.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, 266, page 276 in e-court. And again if you can tell us the date of this photo and what's significant about it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely the date but, it was at least one year after since each time I would return I would retake a picture to see the slow destruction of the monument, and this one -- on this one we can see that only one large piece of concrete is still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page. This is 267 in the hard copy and 277 in e-court. Is this just a close-up of the previous image that we were looking at?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's only a close-up, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page, please, 269 -- my apologies, 268 in the hard copy, and 278 in e-court. Do you recall when --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm wondering whether this is something that the witness should be able to answer and know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll hear from the witness, Mr. Karadzic. What is the question, Mr. Mitchell?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: My first question is: Do you recall what date this particular image was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the date, but the year was 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And my second question is: What is the yellow arrow pointing to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The yellow arrow that I added pinpoints the location where before was the mosque, the central mosque of Srebrenica. This is at this stage being transformed into a parking lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Next page, please, 269 in the hard copy, 279 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another mosque of Srebrenica that is on the way going or returning to Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what date was this photo taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At some point in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Well, this is a separate mosque from the one in the centre of town; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's one of -- in total there were three mosques, but I didn't specifically photograph all of them. This one happened to be on the road to Zeleni Jadar. This is why we could also see what was happening with -- with that one. But I only take -- took the pictures in 1997 of this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, do you recall if this mosque can be seen on any footage from July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I'd now like to read a summary of Dr. Haglund's testimony from the Krstic case. In 1996, Dr. Haglund oversaw the exhumation and examination of human remains from Srebrenica-related mass graves at Cerska, Lazete 2, and Pilica, which is also known as the Branjevo Military Farm. The first site, at Cerska, was a primary undisturbed mass grave located on an embankment by the side of a dirt road. It contained the bodies of 150 males, 149 of whom died of gunshot wounds. Forty-eight ligatures were recovered from the grave, 24 of which were still in place. The individuals with ligatures were randomly disbursed throughout the grave. Based on his examination of the site, including the presence of cartridges along the opposite side of the road to the grave, Dr. Haglund concluded that the victims were lined up along the side of the road and shot and then either fell or were rolled down the embankment. Dirt was then taken from the opposite side of the road and used to cover up the bodies. The second site, known as Lazete 2, was located in a field behind a raised railway track underpass. The field was accessed by a small, rural road which passed through the railway underpass. Dr. Haglund located two deposits of bodies at this site which were designated as Lazete 2A and Lazete 2B. Due to the unseasonably rainy weather, he was unable to determine whether these two deposits were located in two separate pits or in one large trench. Lazete 2A was an undisturbed primary grave which contained 112 relatively complete male bodies, plus one set of remains on the surface. Lazete 2B was a disturbed primary grave which contained a minimum number of 52 individuals. This gave a minimum number of 165 individuals for the site of whom 158 died of gunshot wounds. A total of 104 blindfolds were also recovered from these remains. The third site, known as Pilica, or the Branjevo Military Farm, was a very large grave measuring 28 metres long, 5 metres wide, and 3 metres deep. Only 14 per cent of the grave was occupied by human remains which amounted to a minimum number of 132 individuals. Seventy-seven of these individuals had their hands bound behind their backs, including one individual who had an artificial leg. Dr. Haglund also explained the procedure once the exhumed remains reached the morgue. There, the remains were photographed and passed through a fluoroscope to identify any projectiles. The pathologist would then conduct an autopsy during which clothing was removed as well as evidence to be processed by the evidence technicians and photographers. Forensic anthropologists would also assist in the reconstruction of damaged bones and the determination of sex, age, and the minimum number of individuals. Lastly, Dr. Haglund testified about the findings of an expert panel that was convened by the Office of the Prosecutor to look into criticisms of his work and that of the chief forensic pathologist during the 1996 season. The expert panel found that the criticisms of Dr. Haglund's work did not jeopardise its scientific validity. However, the panel found that the chief pathologist had acted inappropriately by changing the cause of death in some autopsy reports without consulting the pathologist who had conducted the autopsy. Dr. Haglund recalled that the panel considered that the Office of the Prosecutor had handled this situation appropriately by taking all of the autopsy reports back to the original pathologist for review and verification of the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I go to page 7 in e-court in both the English and the B/C/S. utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I want to move now to a few questions regarding Dr. Kirschner. If you can just briefly tell us who Dr. Kirschner was?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So he was the chief forensic pathologist?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I move to page 10 now of this report in both English and B/C/S. And we can see that this is the opinion and comments by Dr. Vincent DiMaio. Can you tell the Court who Dr. Vincent DiMaio is?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Yes. He is a very well-known pathologist from Texas, Dallas, Texas, and I think he was head of this committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We can see in the very stop paragraph on this page that Dr. Kirschner's conduct was considered to be unacceptable. You're aware of that; correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And if I can direct you now to the third paragraph on that page which states: "While Dr. Kirschner's actions had the potential to invalidate or at least taint the autopsy reports, the Tribunal prevented this by submitting the reports back to the original physicians for their certification of cause and manner of death. Therefore, the panel feels no permanent injury to the validity of the reports was effected by the actions of Dr. Kirschner." Now, are you aware of these steps that were taken by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Basically all -- what many -- what happened was there was a sort -- sort of irregular how the pathologist would sign the final cause of death. Some people would give the number of bullets and some people would just say multiple gunshot wounds, and I think that Dr. Kirschner was trying to get it more in that multiple gunshot wound thing and so that's how he changed some of those things. That's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And do you recall who on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor was involved in taking the reports back to the original physicians to certify the cause and manner of death?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Yes. I think that was -- Mr. McCloskey did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That's Peter McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Yes. Peter McCloskey, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Could I go to page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I go to page 8 now in both English and B/C/S. And this is the last questions I want to ask you on this topic. I want to read you the first recommendation of the panel and then I'll see if you have any comment on it: "The evidence of war crimes is overwhelming at each site. A few problems of administration or temporary lapses from a scientific ideal could not jeopardise the overall quality of the evidence and its interpretation at autopsy. Any prosecution of war crimes in Yugoslavia will be on firm scientific grounds. There are literally hundreds of war crime remains that were removed and interpreted by very scientifically sound methods." Doctor, could you have any comment on that recommendation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: I agree with that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's move now to your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mitchell, instead of responding to answer the question in a, so to speak, partial manner, could I ask the doctor what happened with respect to the issue that you just dealt with, in just -- in a comprehensive manner so that the Bench can understand what -- what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Certainly. The report itself goes into a lot of detail, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: But, of course, Dr. Haglund's available to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the question is how things were rectified as far as Dr. Kirschner was concerned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And how the commission was formed and what --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commission was formed by the Tribunal, and they were both anthropologists and pathologists there. They were surprised when they talked to me that there weren't more complaints when you have people from all over the world and they do things different, but of -- but it was the changing of what doctors had written on their report, on this numbering things of the number of gunshot wounds, et cetera, and that was, I think, that was the problem that Dr. Kirschner had with this but not asking these people. People would come in for two weeks and go away. They were -- they were donating their time, and so they may be two weeks -- they could get -- they're good pathologists, and they had to get back to work. They couldn't stay here for all the time, whereas in 1995, they started paying people money. These people were volunteering. We paid their way, paid for their food, paid for place to stay, but they were donating their time. They didn't get paid like everybody did after 1995. They volunteered. So -- and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give us some examples how the numbers were changed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's say a person had been shot 15 times, and then somebody else was shot 2 times, and somebody else was shot 4 times and 5 times. So when you're trying to put that in a -- trying to summarise things, it's better to say single gunshot wound or multiple gunshot -- gunshot wounds, and that was what Dr. Kirschner was trying to get around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you, Doctor. If a person received two gunshot wounds, could that be classified as multiple?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: To round this off, Doctor, you've talked about -- that was the issue with Dr. Kirschner?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: There were also some allegations about you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Perhaps you'd briefly expand on that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: There were three or four people, I think, that had. I think the biggest concern that some people had that they thought that there was so many -- maybe you could -- should only take out two bodies a day, or three bodies a day or -- and they're used to working with skeletal remains, and yes, when you're dealing with skeletal remains it's going to take a while because you have to deal with 206 bones and you have to clean all off and move them, but when you have bodies in the conditions we had, they were most the part complete remains and they -- they were all -- in a lot of times they were all connected together. It was just to get them out from the pile of bodies that they were integrated with and covered partially with another body, et cetera, and -- and it is -- and it also depends upon how the bodies are scattered. If -- like in the Cerska grave, when we had 30 metres by 6 metres, and you had 150 people, sometimes they rolled upon each other, but you had enough room to get -- there's enough room to get several -- two -- a two-person team to go in and start working on exposing those remains where you could move them. If you're in a very small area then you can't do that. So those were problematic things we just run into doing graves all the time. And if you have bodies that are fleshed and total and they're at the bottom of the grave when you get there, you could take out 20 a day or 40 a day. The -- the problem with that is -- is the mapping, because we map where the head is, where the shoulders were, where the elbows, where the hands were, where the knees were, where the hips were, where the feet were. But if you have somebody doing a total station, and electronically doing that, if you have a good person running that, in three minutes they have it done, and then basically what you have to do is get the body so they can lift it, put it in a bag, number it and take it out of the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And so the criticisms of you were primarily related to just the speed at which the exhumations had been done.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Yeah. I think three or four people thought that was bad, so -- but they were used to working in -- mostly with skeletal remains and -- and it did take a long time, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Let's move to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I think now you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Doctor, we're going to move now to look at your findings for the Cerska site. If I can have Exhibit P00209 in e-court. Doctor, this is a photo of the Cerska site that you were shown in the Krstic case. And what I'd like to ask you to do is if you could briefly explain to the Court what your conclusions are about what happened at this site, and if you want to mark the image, that may be helpful as well.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Well, you can't see a whole lot of the image. It's really dark on one side. I hope there's another slide that shows that side, because this is -- but basically it was a winding road going up the Cerska Valley, a gravel road. The -- the hillside had been cut when they made the road originally, and we found this area where there was new growth coming up. It had just probably grown a year and it was on like the others, and we found that that actually was a grave. It was a 30-metre long grave and 6 metres down an incline. There were groups of shell casings that come from automatic rifles when they're spit out and they'll go into piles if person stands in the same -- same place on the opposite side of the road next to where the road had been cut and -- and the victims were lined up along the far side of the grave. It would be on the -- the -- where you see the vegetation, lined up there, and then they were shot in a sort of a spray pattern. People were -- the killers were -- with automatic weapon, they were just shooting around and so they could just sort of spray. That's what the pathologists call it, that pattern. Then at some point the bodies either fell or were rolled over the side of the embankment, and then they had a machine, and they took more gravel -- gravelly soil off from the side of the embankment that had been cut when they made the road and then they had covered up the bodies in a sort of a superficial way, and that was -- the soil was made of small pebbles, and it wasn't very much piled on top of the bodies, so the bodies, when we got there, they -- a lot of them were partially skeletalised. They heated up in the sun, and it was -- and the -- with the rocks in there also made it like that, and so this grave had a lot of skeletal exposure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you. Doctor, I want to turn your attention now to the Lazete 2 site. If we can have 65 ter 2458 in e-court. We're going to see a diagram of your exhumations at the Lazete 2 site. And if I can ask you to mark some things on this diagram.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Up here by the grave. It's hard to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If you could explain or talk us through your exhumation of this site, and if you need to mark anything, please do so.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Well, there's a road down here, and where the railroad comes through there's a little road that goes along here. It goes under that railroad. This is an area that's coming down from hills, and this is a drainage area. This whole area is a drainage area. In fact, there had been a lot of movement of big machinery over this area, so it was really all mud because we got into the rainy season. Going up this area here is where the actual grave was. So we started doing trenches across this way, this way, and then finally we found -- we ran into -- we did that at equidistant, and then we found where the graves, the remains were. They were all -- the depth was about 2.5 to 3 metres. This is Lazete A, and this is Lazete B. This A had not been disturbed. People come back to dig a grave, but they weren't the ones who put the bodies in the grave, and they just started digging in this one area here and did their business, which wasn't very good, and I hope that we get to see some photograph here. There was, I believe, a hundred and -- there was 132 in that one grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Doctor, if --

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: There was a hundred -- yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what you're looking at at the moment?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Well, when I find it, I'll let you know. The A, B -- the A grave was an undisturbed grave. The B grave was a disturbed grave where bodies had been removed and taken somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is that binder -- I'm sorry. One second. What is that binder that you've got in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: It has from the reports, just the first volume of the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: This grave A had 112 individuals, and grave B had a residual, sometimes not very many complete bodies of 52 individuals in that grave. And then there were 98 separately documented ones from the B grave that were just pieces. There would be bones, fractured bones, maybe an arm, maybe a leg and -- but minimal number there was 52 individuals. So all told, we had 164 individuals from both graves and one -- when we'd done the assessment, we found one surface remains, and we had just put it shallowly and buried it there, and so there were 165 remains that we took from that site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where can we find in your report of that explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: The -- actually, just the numbers on that are from page -- it's -- it's part of the introduction. It's executive summary. It's ix, 9.

utterances.text: Doctor, if I can just ask you to -- the road that you marked on there, can you put an A next to that, the letter A.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.text: And the main road to the right of the picture, put a B next to that.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM HAGLUND
utterances.text: Yes. And there's also another grave down here also, but it was flooded. We didn't want to take this one. This was the less flooded that we had.
